identity.title: AutoEP: LLMs-Driven Automation of Hyperparameter Evolution for Metaheuristic Algorithms

problem.claim: Dynamically configuring hyperparameters for metaheuristic algorithms is a fundamental computational-intelligence challenge.

gap.claim: Learning-based automation methods are described as limited by prohibitive sample complexity and poor generalization.

contributions.claim: AutoEP uses LLMs as zero-shot reasoning engines for algorithm control, avoiding training.
The framework combines online Exploratory Landscape Analysis for real-time quantitative search feedback with a multi-LLM reasoning chain that generates adaptive hyperparameter strategies.
The authors present grounding LLM reasoning in empirical search data as a way to mitigate hallucination and describe an accessible paradigm for automated hyperparameter design.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors identify AutoEP's tight integration of online ELA and multi-LLM reasoning, together with training-free zero-shot control, as its core innovation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AutoEP consistently outperforms state-of-the-art tuners, including neural-evolution and other LLM-based methods, across three metaheuristics and diverse combinatorial-optimization benchmarks.
The authors report that the open-source Qwen3-30B matches GPT-4 in performance within their framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic hyperparameter configuration is framed as a fundamental challenge.
Existing learning-based automation is characterized as sample-inefficient and weakly generalizing.
AutoEP replaces training with zero-shot LLM reasoning, coordinated with online ELA feedback and adaptive strategy generation.
The authors report gains over several tuner classes and parity between Qwen3-30B and GPT-4.

source_observation.claim: AutoEP connects high-level LLM reasoning to real-time quantitative search feedback to mitigate hallucination.

lessons.interpretation: A claim about reasoning-based control can be made more concrete by explicitly tying decisions to measured process signals.
lessons.application: For an adaptive algorithm, define an online diagnostic module and show how each diagnostic informs the controller's next action.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when reliable online diagnostics are unavailable or their computation materially disrupts the optimization process.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark identities, evaluation metrics, baselines, statistical variation, or the meaning of “consistently.”
The conditions under which Qwen3-30B matches GPT-4, including prompting, resources, and tasks, are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide details needed to assess the reported mitigation of hallucination or the claimed generalization.
